Build the Regions Table and Filter(s) for One Scan Unit

Source: R/build_scan_regions.R
build_scan_regions.Rd

Region dispatch for the unified GLOW scan. Returns the per-chromosome regions table plus the variant filter(s) for a single scan unit (a chromosome for gene/coding, a genome chunk for window). This is the one structural fork of the scan: gene/window run a single filter over many regions, while coding runs many filters (one per category) over the same regions, so the return carries either one filter object or a named category -> filter map.

build_scan_regions(
  region_type,
  chr,
  config,
  chunk = NULL,
  variant_index = NULL,
  gds_path = NULL
)

Arguments

region_type

Character: one of "gene", "window", "coding", "noncoding".

chr

Integer or character chromosome.

config

An environment or named list of resolved config values. Fields used per type: filter_spec (all); resolved_gene_list (optional, gene); window_size, step_size (window); categories (coding).

chunk

A single-row data.frame (one row of the genome-chunk table) for region_type = "window"; ignored otherwise. Must carry chunk_start, chunk_end, span_end. Default NULL.

variant_index

A glow_variant_index of the unit's GDS from GLOWr::build_variant_index(), or NULL (default). Used by region_type = "gene", for the large-gene segmentation below, and by "noncoding", whose candidate lists are row numbers in it (built from gds_path when NULL).

gds_path

Character path of the unit's GDS/aGDS, or NULL (default). Required for region_type = "noncoding"; ignored by the others.

Value

A named list:

regions

A data.frame with at least chr, start, end, label (the define_regions_* shape); for noncoding, a NAMED list of such tables, one per mask, each with the n_records, category, gene_rank and variant_rows columns of GLOWr::define_regions_noncoding.

filters

A single glow_variant_filter (gene/window) OR a named list mapping each category label to a glow_variant_filter (coding, noncoding).

Details

region_type = "gene". regions is GLOWr::define_regions_gene(chr = chr) — the bundled STAARpipeline gene table for the chromosome — unless config$resolved_gene_list is present (a user-supplied custom gene list), in which case that list is subset to chr. filters is the single filter do.call(GLOWr::variant_filter, config$filter_spec).

region_type = "window". Requires a chunk row (one row of the genome-chunk table from define_genome_chunks, with chunk_start, chunk_end, span_end). regions is GLOWr::define_regions_window(chr, chunk$chunk_start, chunk$span_end, config$window_size, config$step_size) trimmed by the sliding boundary rule (keep start <= chunk$chunk_end): windows are generated to the chromosome span_end so boundary-spanning windows are kept, then only those owned by this chunk (start within [chunk_start, chunk_end]) are retained, so the union of chunks equals one full-span slide. filters is the single variant_filter from config$filter_spec.

region_type = "coding". regions is the chromosome gene table (as for gene). filters is a NAMED list mapping each category label to its resolved glow_variant_filter: config$categories is either a character vector of builtin coding category names (each resolved via GLOWr::coding_filter) or a named list mapping labels to a builtin name OR a list of custom DNF annotation clauses (resolved via GLOWr::variant_filter with the run's filter_spec). The MAF/MAC/min-variant axes come from config$filter_spec so a category never hardcodes them.

region_type = "noncoding". The gene-centric non-coding masks (see GLOWr::define_regions_noncoding). Needs gds_path, because the regions come from the chromosome's annotations, not from gene coordinates: the chromosome's QC, type, category and presence vectors are read once, and for every mask in config$noncoding_categories (default GLOWr::noncoding_masks(), the eight masks) one regions table is built whose rows are the genes with linked records and whose variant_rows column lists each gene's candidate records. regions is then a NAMED list of those tables, one per mask, and filters the matching map of GLOWr::noncoding_filter(mask, run filter) (the run's filter with no annotation clause). The GDS handle is closed on return.

Large-gene segmentation (gene)

At whole-genome-sequencing density a gene body can hold tens of thousands of records, and the per-gene cost and memory grow with the square of the variant count. When variant_index is supplied and config$gene_max_records is a finite number, every gene's GDS records inside its span are counted from the index (before any filter, so the count depends only on the file), and a gene with more records than that is replaced by non-overlapping segments of config$gene_segment_bp base pairs (default 10,000) that start at the gene start; the last segment ends at the gene end. Each segment is its own region row with the gene's region_id, its own start and end, and label = <gene label>_seg<k>, and it is tested and reported like a gene; there is no gene-level combination of the segments. A gene whose span fits one segment is left as it is. The returned table then also carries n_records (the index count of each row) and the attributes n_genes_segmented and n_segments. With variant_index NULL, or gene_max_records NULL or infinite, nothing is segmented.

See also

GLOWr::define_regions_gene, GLOWr::define_regions_window, GLOWr::variant_filter, GLOWr::coding_filter, run_scan_unit

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
env <- new.env(); source("runs/myrun/config.R", local = env)
# Gene: one filter, the chr gene table.
g <- build_scan_regions("gene", chr = 22, config = env)
# Window: trimmed to the chunk boundary.
chunk <- define_genome_chunks(22, window_size = env$window_size,
                              step_size = env$step_size)[1, ]
w <- build_scan_regions("window", chr = 22, config = env, chunk = chunk)
# Coding: a category -> filter map.
co <- build_scan_regions("coding", chr = 22, config = env)
names(co$filters)
# Non-coding: one regions table per mask, from the chromosome's annotations.
nc <- build_scan_regions("noncoding", chr = 22, config = env,
                         gds_path = "data/chr22.gds")
sapply(nc$regions, nrow)
} # }
